task.question: What was the magnitude of the earthquake that struck the Kumamoto area of Japan in July 2026?
task.evidence: July 28 – A magnitude 7.1 earthquake hits Kumamoto Prefecture, killing 39 people.

Ты решаешь задачи. Если нужно посчитать или найти факт, вызывай инструменты, а не угадывай.
Когда ответ готов, напиши его последней строкой в формате FINAL: <ответ>.
Формат ответа в FINAL: только сама сущность — имя, число, название, место или дата, не длиннее пяти слов. На языке вопроса.
Не добавляй ничего, о чём не спросили напрямую: к дате не приписывай год, если вопрос не просит именно год; к городу не приписывай страну или регион; не оборачивай ответ в предложение и не поясняй его.
Пример: если вопрос про дату события — FINAL: 15 September, а не FINAL: 15 September, 2026. Если вопрос про место — FINAL: New Delhi, а не FINAL: New Delhi, India.
Для числовых задач в FINAL только число.
What was the magnitude of the earthquake that struck the Kumamoto area of Japan in July 2026?

[2026 Kumamoto earthquake]

On 28 July 2026 at approximately 16:27:15 JST (07:27:15 UTC), an earthquake struck Kumamoto Prefecture in southern Japan with a magnitude of Mww 6.8 (MJMA 7.1) at a depth of 10 km (6.2 mi), later revised to 16 km (9.9 mi). At least 38 people were killed and more than 368 were injured.

The Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) has officially named the earthquake the 2026 Kumamoto earthquake (Japanese: 令和8年熊本地震, Hepburn: Reiwa 8-nen Kumamoto jishin).

Earthquake

The earthquake occurred at 16:27 JST (07:27 UTC) on 28 July in Kumamoto Prefecture, Japan. According to the Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA), the earthquake had a magnitude of MJMA 7.1. The United States Geological Survey (USGS) recorded an earthquake of Mww 6.8 with an epicenter 3 km (1.9 mi) west-southwest of the city of Uki. It was caused by strike‑slip faulting. The USGS focal mechanism solution suggested coseismic slip occurred on either a northwest-trending left‑lateral fault or a northeast-trending right‑lateral fault.

Geology

Kumamoto Prefecture is located on Kyushu, the most southerly of Japan's four main islands. It lies at the southern end of the Japan Median Tectonic Line, Japan's longest, where a system of active faults forks in two directions at the Beppu-Haneyama fault zone. Earthquakes occur along the Beppu–Shimabara graben, with epicenters moving from west to east over time.
